group_assessment.weighting: PubMed ESearch 2026-10-02: Richards RI[au] 149 records, 9 intersecting WWOX. The Adelaide fragile-site group built and published the Drosophila WWOX model itself and is the primary group for WWOX in Drosophila, which is why its ROS premise is self-cited rather than measured here. It is not a neurological or clinical WWOX group: its frame is cancer and genome instability throughout.

field_density.note: Eleven WWOX-and-Drosophila records exist and this group authored most of them, so the fly WWOX literature is close to a single-group literature; agreement within it is weaker evidence than it looks.

multihop.enumeration_method: All 70 references enumerated from the JATS deposit; 35 mention WWOX or FRA16D. One is resolved by PMID here and only one, because it is the dependency the integrity screen flagged (Fabbri 2005, PMID 16223882, expression of concern) and resolving it was required to state its citing_relation. The remaining WWOX-mentioning references are background citations that carry no measurement into this paper and are not opened as hops by this reading.

entries.proposition: Reducing WWOX suppresses TNFalpha-induced cell death in vivo; the direction is loss-protects.
entries.snippet: resulted in suppression of the Egr/TNF
entries.anchor: Results, Altered WWOX modulates ectopic Egr/TNFalpha eye phenotypes, para 1 (sentence continues 'alpha-mediated rough eye phenotype')

entries.proposition: The ROS link is explicitly a hypothesis carried from the group's earlier work, not a measurement in this paper.
entries.snippet: a likely mechanism by which WWOX contributes to the Egr/TNF
entries.anchor: Discussion, para 5 (the sentence continues with the Egr/TNFalpha-mediated cell death pathway being via its regulation of ROS)

entries.proposition: A complete Drosophila WWOX null is viable to adulthood, which bounds how much a negative result in this organism can say about a human biallelic-loss phenotype.
entries.snippet: or where WWOX function is completely removed (trans-heterozygous for independent WWOX alleles)
entries.anchor: Results, Requirement for WWOX tumor suppressor activity in vivo, final paragraph

entries.proposition: Ectopic WWOX alone produces no phenotype; the modulation appears only under stress.
entries.snippet: Ectopic expression of WWOX alone does not result in any obvious cell death-induced phenotype
entries.anchor: Results, Altered WWOX modulates ectopic Egr/TNFalpha eye phenotypes, para 2

entries.proposition: The most severely affected discs were excluded from the clonal quantification, and the exclusion falls far more heavily on the knockdown arm than on the control arm.
entries.snippet: Significant disruption to eye disc morphology was observed in 13/52 pairs of the Scrib
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods, Clonal analyses (sentence continues with the 31/50 figure for the WWOX-IR clones)

entries.proposition: The paper's own text and figure legend both state that decreasing WWOX decreases the caspase-3 area, and that increasing WWOX increases it.
entries.snippet: Conversely, increased WWOX expression increased the relative area of Caspase 3 staining
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX modifies Caspase 3 staining in response to ectopic Egr/TNFalpha

entries.proposition: The only quantification supporting that claim is labelled in the opposite sense: in the plot, the up-WWOX column is the lower one and the down-WWOX column the higher one.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 5 panel G, 'Relative area of Caspase 3', carries three x-axis columns labelled (left to right) 'up-TNFa control', 'up-TNFa up-WWOX' and 'up-TNFa down-WWOX', with means at about 21.5, 18 and 24 percent and brackets marked ** over control-versus-up-WWOX and * over control-versus-down-WWOX.
entries.anchor: Figure 5, panel G; native JPEG inspected
entries.contradicts_needle: increased WWOX expression increased the relative area of Caspase 3 staining

entries.proposition: A single heterozygous loss-of-function allele measurably shifts the endpoint, which makes this a true in-vivo gene-dosage assay rather than an all-or-nothing knockout comparison.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Supplementary Figure 1 panel F, 'Adult eye size', plots three genotypes - wild type, WWOX1/+ and WWOX2/+ - at about 26, 29 and 32 times ten to the fourth pixels, with drawn brackets marked * and **** respectively; panel I shows the empty-vector lane at essentially zero Wwox/Tubulin signal while the ORF and cDNA lanes sit at about 0.33 and 0.35.
entries.anchor: Supplementary Figure 1, panels F and I; layered TIFF flattened (composite layer) and inspected

entries.proposition: The supplementary eye-size result supporting 'WWOX contributes to low-level Egr/TNF-alpha cell death' is that adult eyes of Wwox heterozygotes are larger than wild type under Egr/TNF-alpha expression.
entries.snippet: This indicates that WWOX can contribute to low level Egr/TNFα-mediated cell death.
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX contributes to Egr/TNFalpha-mediated cell death, with S1 Fig
